name: Byzantine recovery attempts
summary: After the catastrophic defeat at Manzikert (1071), the Byzantine Empire enters a decade of civil war between competing claimants for the throne, Romanos IV Diogenes (captured by the Seljuks then released), Michael VII Doukas, Nikephoros III Botaneiates, and finally Alexios I Komnenos (1081). While Byzantine factions fight each other, the Seljuk Turks colonize virtually all of Anatolia, the agricultural and military heartland that had supplied the empire with three-quarters of its tax revenue and most of its soldiers. By 1081, the empire's Anatolian frontier has collapsed from the Euphrates to within 50 miles of Constantinople.

_quarry.structural_significance: The decade of civil war following Manzikert is more damaging than the battle itself; the permanent loss of Anatolia transforms Byzantium from a great empire into a rump state dependent on western mercenaries; it is the direct cause of Alexios I's appeal to Rome that launches the First Crusade
